input: Learn to make fresh pasta from scratch

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Fresh pasta covers a huge range — basic egg dough tagliatelle vs. stuffed pasta like ravioli vs. shaped pasta like orecchiette require very different techniques and time investments.
Cooking for one person learning solo is very different from cooking for a family or hosting guests, which affects batch size, complexity, and how the learning is structured.
Kitchen equipment available (stand mixer, pasta machine, rolling pin only) dramatically changes the method and which recipes are feasible.
How much time the user can dedicate per session shapes whether they should start with a quick weeknight recipe or a more involved weekend project.
Whether the user wants to learn through written recipes, video tutorials, a class, or hands-on experimentation determines the entire learning path.
The definition of success — making one reliable pasta type confidently vs. mastering multiple styles vs. impressing guests at a dinner party — sets the ambition level and end goal of the plan.

Knowing their current cooking skill level clarifies where to start — a complete beginner needs foundational knife and dough skills, while an experienced cook can skip basics and focus on pasta-specific technique.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to make fresh pasta from scratch
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn how to make fresh pasta from scratch, covering the full process from dough to finished noodles.

questions.title: Which pasta type do you want to learn first?

questions.title: Who will you be cooking this pasta for?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is cooking solo, for a household, or for guests, which affects portion sizes, complexity, and how the learning sessions should be structured.

questions.title: What pasta-making equipment do you already own?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a pasta machine, stand mixer, or only basic tools like a rolling pin and knife, as this dictates which methods and recipes are feasible.

questions.title: How much time can you dedicate to each practice session?
questions.description: Understand the user's available time per session to determine whether the plan should focus on quick weeknight-friendly recipes or longer weekend projects.

questions.title: How do you prefer to learn a new cooking skill?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred learning style — written recipes, video tutorials, an in-person class, or trial-and-error experimentation — to choose the right resources and format.

questions.title: What does success look like when you have nailed this?
questions.description: Clarify the user's end goal — confidently making one pasta type, mastering several styles, or being able to cook it for guests — to set the right ambition level for the plan.

questions.title: How confident are you in the kitchen right now?
questions.description: Gauge the user's current cooking experience level to determine the starting point — whether to include foundational dough-handling basics or jump straight into pasta-specific techniques.
